samples.marker: Jinja PoC: regression fixture; preserve whoami execution signatures
evidence: The JSON contains a single template expression, derived from the pyLoad CVE-2024-32880 demonstration quoted in the tracked GHSA-3f7w-p8vr-4v5f advisory.

Unsandboxed Jinja 3.1.6 resolves undefined x to an Undefined object, follows its Python __init__.__globals__, indexes __builtins__ and eval, imports os, calls popen(whoami), and reads the command output. The command was intercepted, not launched.
SandboxedEnvironment blocks __init__ access. The JSON itself has no renderer, target, request driver, install hook or autonomous trigger.

The file is byte-identical to a regression control created by tracked commit 41e9cca37a0ce91b03527627ce24438eaf6fb3ca. This verified testing purpose and the non-destructive whoami probe tip the verdict; execution-capable exploit syntax remains accurately detected.

samples.identification: Synthetic fsspec version-1 Jinja injection regression payload
samples.marker: fsspec PoC: regression fixture; x binding blocks command execution
evidence: The version-1 reference set has empty refs and dimensions, a template named x, and a generator URL containing the same globals/builtins/eval/popen expression.

Inspected fsspec 2026.4.0 ReferenceFileSystem._process_references1, _process_templates and _process_gen. _process_templates wraps the template in a lambda and binds x to that callable; an empty dimension map still produces one generator iteration.

Rendering gen.url follows x.__init__, which is a method-wrapper without __globals__. The exact sample raises UndefinedError before eval or popen. Interception verified zero command calls; no URL fetch occurred.
The same expression can execute under another unsandboxed binding context, so failure in this tested consumer does not invalidate its injection signatures.

The bytes exactly match the synthetic reference-set regression fixture from tracked commit 41e9cca37a0ce91b03527627ce24438eaf6fb3ca. Testing provenance plus the failed exact consumer path favor BENIGN.

samples.identification: Malformed HTML/JavaScript carrier for escaped PHP webshell signatures
samples.marker: PHP upload fixture: malformed test carrier; preserve shell patterns
evidence: The page explicitly calls itself a minimal regression carrier. It constructs a Content-Disposition filename parameter, a double-escaped PHP request-to-system expression and a Blob passed to xhr.send.

QuickJS 1.19.4 rejects the full script: HTML-style <!-- comments end at the newline, leaving the following comment text as invalid JavaScript. xhr is also never constructed or opened and no target is configured.

Evaluating only the string construction leaves literal backslash-x3c and backslash-x3e delimiters and escaped quotes around cmd. These are not executable PHP bytes. The static decoder produces a 45-byte PHP-like child with flow-graph-limited and flow-query-incomplete diagnostics; this is signature evidence rather than proof of transmitted or runnable source.
The embedded pattern is system($_GET[cmd]) with echo output: a command webshell if correctly reconstructed and deployed. Its request-command and output signatures remain.

The file is byte-identical to the explicitly constructed control added in tracked commit 652470bb0a90f67aa2ff08fef11d930d554843ca. Test provenance, malformed code and absent driver favor BENIGN; failed execution alone is not the verdict criterion.

conclusions: No broad form/http/communications ancestor selectors consume the moved rule in the current YAML tree.

Audited 25 upload-directory consumers. Most binary or non-overlapping language scopes cannot observe this HTML/PHP/JavaScript atom. Applicable consumers use upload as transport/API evidence, except an anti-analysis upload exclusion. A filename parameter supplies neither transport nor an upload operation, so those selectors intentionally do not gain a form alternative.

No behavioral rule is deleted or demoted. A lone PHP filename continues to emit a notable form observation and cannot stand in for an upload operation. Retained real CSRF-upload and escaped-shell controls preserve their hostile chain findings.
